Both files exist. The container ID is `2e0193c40cde`. Here's how to copy them to your Windows machine:

**Step 1 — Open a WSL terminal on your Windows machine** (outside the Docker container).

**Step 2 — Copy from the container to WSL:**

```bash
docker cp 2e0193c40cde:/tmp/holo/phase7_topview_zigzag_hybrid_path_w_root.mp4 ~/Videos/
docker cp "2e0193c40cde:/tmp/holo/phase7_topview_sine_hybrid_path_snA1_snwx1p571_hmpolyline_nspl256_pref_ramp_trn1_toff0_w_root.mp4" ~/Videos/
```

This copies them to your WSL home directory under `~/Videos/` (create the folder first with `mkdir -p ~/Videos` if it doesn't exist, or change the destination to any path you prefer like `~/`).

**Step 3 — Access them from Windows:**

Your WSL filesystem is visible from Windows Explorer at:
```
\\wsl$\Ubuntu\home\<your-wsl-username>\Videos\
```
(Replace `Ubuntu` with your actual WSL distro name if different.)

Or you can copy them directly to a Windows path from WSL:

```bash
docker cp 2e0193c40cde:/tmp/holo/phase7_topview_zigzag_hybrid_path_w_root.mp4 /mnt/c/Users/<YourWindowsUsername>/Videos/
docker cp "2e0193c40cde:/tmp/holo/phase7_topview_sine_hybrid_path_snA1_snwx1p571_hmpolyline_nspl256_pref_ramp_trn1_toff0_w_root.mp4" /mnt/c/Users/<YourWindowsUsername>/Videos/
```

Replace `<YourWindowsUsername>` with your actual Windows username. The `/mnt/c/` prefix maps to your `C:\` drive.
